text:
Why have you come now,

youth,

life's brazen enchantment?

What brings you to the beach?

We older people were at peace

and you come to wound us, reviving

the most frightening impossible dreams,

you come to prod our imaginations.


Risen from the waves,

all shimmer, radiance, pure sensation

and the undulations of an animal lying in wait,

you advance toward shore

with tiny pink breasts,

with buttocks as mischievous as smiles,

O slender goddess with thick ankles,

and with that suggestion

(so very much your own)

of the belly giving way to the beginning

of the thighs: delicate beauty,

precise and indecisive,

where one might rest one's forehead and shed tears.


And we watch you come—vision

of a fabulous stretch of shore

with bulls, conch shells and dolphins,

on the soft sand between sea and sky,

still trembling with droplets,

dazzled by the sun and smiling.


You herald the kingdom of life,

the dream of another life, more intense and freer,

without desire festering like remorse

—without desire for you, sophisticated

little beast of a child, in whom meet

the starlet's straightforward beauty

and the prince's graceful shyness.


Though suddenly you furrow

the brow tormented by a thought

both touching and obtuse,

and turning to the sea your face, where

among wet blond locks shines

the melancholy expression of Antinous,

O indifferent beauty,

you walk along the beach as if unaware

that men and dogs follow you,

gods and angels,

and archangels,

thrones, abominations…

translation.title: Why Have You Come Now...
